A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered theorems.

before.justification: Section 3 and Figures 1–2 report original Gaussian-token simulations measuring angular contraction and normalized Jacobian norms.

after.justification: Section 3 retains these original simulations and both result figures. The added Appendix D is theoretical.

M1.justification: The normalized attention model, identity key/query/value matrices, logarithmic scaling, and residual update in Equations (2.1)–(2.3) are unchanged. The added theoretical discussions do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Gaussian-token setting. The Gaussian-score model in new Appendix D is analyzed mathematically, without adding an evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally compares competing methods. YaRN, Qwen, SSMax, and SWAN-GPT remain contextual examples in the unchanged Table 1.

E3.justification: Section 3 retains the same token generation, single-layer evaluation without residual connections or MLPs, dimensions 2, 32, and 512, parameter sweeps, and metrics in Equations (3.2)–(3.3).

E4.justification: The existing analyses across dimension, correlation, and scaling are retained. No new empirical ablation or robustness test accompanies the added exact-tie discussion or Gaussian theoretical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the Hutchinson trace estimator for Figure 2. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The six heatmap panels in Figures 1–2 have identical plotted values. The reported contraction and gradient trends, including sharper transitions at larger dimensions, are unchanged; no empirical result entries are added.

T1.justification: New Appendix D adds Gaussian order-statistic limits, a softmax approximation, and Proposition D.1 with a proof sketch. Remark 2.2 asserts an extension to bounded numbers of exact ties. Appendix C corrects Lemma C.1 and Theorem C.2 to invoke Assumption 3 instead of Assumption 2, while Appendix B expands a derivative calculation. The original main theorems otherwise remain unchanged after renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal logarithmic phase-transition claim remain unchanged. The new conclusion additionally foregrounds order-one top-score gaps as the structural explanation and explicitly emphasizes robustness to near ties.

C2.justification: Appendix D and the conclusion explain the logarithmic versus square-root-logarithmic scaling distinction through geometric versus Gaussian score gaps. Remark 2.2 newly discusses applicability to exact ties, extending the earlier discussion of almost-simplex configurations.

D1.justification: The existing data-generation and estimator descriptions are retained. No implementation settings, hardware, sample counts, runtime information, or code/data access instructions are added or revised.

R1.justification: V2 adds De Haan and Ferreira's extreme-value reference and Rigollet's transformer-dynamics reference. Appendix D develops the already-present contrast with Gaussian/REM models; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 adds a conclusion, acknowledgments, an LLM-use disclosure, and targeted explanatory passages. It also corrects wording, expands equation references, and changes Appendix C's title from 'Median' to 'Middle' phases. Most existing prose and organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are enlarged and placed together on page 12 instead of separate pages. Captions and surrounding layout are adjusted, while panel content, axes, color scales, and Table 1 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The expanded explanations and corrected Appendix C assumption references help presentation, but the additions introduce theoretical defects. Remark 2.2 calls exact ties a special case of Assumption 3, although that assumption excludes off-diagonal exact ties. Appendix D's Equation (D.1) incorrectly gives all successive Gaussian extreme spacings identical Exp(1) limits; their rates depend on rank. These localized correctness problems outweigh the modest exposition gains, with the central theorems and simulations otherwise unchanged.
